Wraped the linkchecker invocation in hack/testing/retry.sh so a transient failure is retried instead of failing CI.

<summary>📝 Walkthrough</summary>

## Walkthrough

`verify.sh` is updated to derive `SOURCE_DIR` from the script's canonical location via `BASH_SOURCE[0]` and `pwd -P`, compute `ROOT_DIR` two levels up, update Docker build/run paths accordingly, and wrap the `docker run` linkchecker invocation with `hack/testing/retry.sh --attempts 5 --delay 5 --stream` to handle transient connection failures.

## Changes

**Linkchecker Script Update**

| Layer / File(s) | Summary |
|---|---|
| **Canonical paths and retry wrapping** <br> `hack/testing/linkchecker/verify.sh` | `SOURCE_DIR` is now computed from `BASH_SOURCE[0]` with `pwd -P` canonicalization; `ROOT_DIR` is set two levels up; Docker build references `SOURCE_DIR`-scoped Dockerfile; the `docker run` invocation is prefixed with `hack/testing/retry.sh --attempts 5 --delay 5 --stream` to retry on transient errors. |

## Estimated code review effort

🎯 1 (Trivial) | ⏱️ ~3 minutes

## Possibly related PRs

- [kubernetes-sigs/kueue#11992](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue/pull/11992): Modifies other CI/test shell scripts to wrap network-dependent steps with `hack/testing/retry.sh`, the same retry mechanism introduced here for the linkchecker.
